title: P104 tooling: lift the input-lift and BIT-pin gate ceilings (signed curvature + admitted BIT pin), Lean lemma
body:
Tooling/framework only. No word, no kappa claim. Package: `research/p104-gate-ceiling-lift`.

## Problem
The official complex-word gate cannot certify any word above two ceilings just over the #7617 frontier (kappa .00365760025222):
- input-lift check: absolute curvature 94.216 caps kappa at -d1/94.216 = .0037765 (+3.24%);
- default BIT pin .00376669 (+2.98%).

## Fix
A patched copy `interval_gate_signed.py` (the pinned `shared-wire-split-composition/interval_gate.py` is not edited; its sha256 is pinned in `frontier7000-source.json`), plus `interval_gate.diff`:
- signed (negative-coefficient) curvature N = 51.137, lift ceiling -d1/N = .006957747;
- default BIT pin = admitted ordinary BIT saving .00385248 (12039/3125000 in `certificates/frontier7000/CLAIM.json`; #7001 admission, README.md:36-37, PROOF-REVIEW.md:389), with `assert cap <= F(BIT_PIN)`.

Certifiable up to kappa < .00385248 - 7g (+5.33% over #7617), instead of .00376669 (+2.98%). The premise keeps the same conditional status (same five assumptions).

## Proof
Since r^-k <= 1, L'' >= -N, so L' >= -d1 - kN > 0 on [0, cap] and L(k) > L(0) = 0; interval upper ends are in the safe direction (README.md).

## Lean
`LiftPositivity.lean`: 0 sorry, standard axioms only. Checked under Lean v4.33 / Mathlib 55b7917; not yet built under the repo pin (v4.21 / Mathlib 308445d). The file carries the repo-pin import `Mathlib.Data.Complex.ExponentialBounds`.

## Tests
`tests/gate_test.py`: 32/32 expected outcomes (original reproduces the #7000 recorded fields; signed gate passes #7000/#7617/#7615; rejects corrupted invoices, tested >= pin, pin above the admitted saving, lift caps above -d1/N, three mutants). `scripts/research_package.py --package research/p104-gate-ceiling-lift` passes. An independent audit found the patch sound; its caveats are applied.

## Caveats
Hard-coded input-lift histogram {7,3,5}/{9,4,1,1} and the five conditional assumptions are inherited; a word that changes its input lifts is not covered. Synthetic invoices test gate logic only. #7617 itself did not run this gate, so claim/tested parameters in the test are ours.
